source_title: Cardiff City news: Speculation over Callum Robinson future 'irrelevant' - BBC
source_excerpt:
Head coach Brian Barry-Murphy says speculation over the Cardiff City future of striker Callum Robinson is "irrelevant".
The 31-year-old has been left out of the Bluebirds squad for the past two games, initially being overlooked for the 2-2 draw at Middlesbrough on 17 October for a breach of internal squad standards.
Despite returning to training he was also absent for the 1-0 win against Birmingham a week later leading to fans questioning whether he has a long-term role at the club.
"All the stuff about speculation, about what's going on in the future is irrelevant to me," said Barry-Murphy.
Robinson, who is contracted to the club until the summer of 2027, has made just nine league starts since the Irishman took charge at the Cardiff City Stadium.
Prior to Barry-Murphy's arrival he was the club's top scorer and player of the season for 2024-25.
But when pressed on Robinson's future prior to Saturday's Championship game at Wolves, Barry-Murphy would not give much away.
"All the players want to play," he added.
"I would like to play them as much as I could but I can only play certain players and try and pick the best team for every game based on what I see."
